business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Distribution of Virgin Polyethylene and Polypropylene Granules

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (National-Level Jurisdiction; no separate sub-state corporate registrar for LLCs)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mixed with Islamic Sharia principles in commercial practice)

Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980, in force 1996)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Decree Law No. 3 of 2015; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, as amended; Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 8 of 2015; Executive Regulations of the AML Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 950 of 2003, as amended); GAFI UBO Disclosure Instructions issued under Companies Law Article 92; EMLCU AML/CFT Compliance Rules for Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and articles of association (extract) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the country of origin is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention) or Egyptian Consular Legalization through the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; otherwise consular authentication at the nearest Egyptian Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport copy and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 25% or more of the Egyptian LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identification authority, passport office or public notary in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC, appointing initial managers, and approving initial capital remittance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate board of directors, company secretary and public notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's reference letter and evidence of source of funds for the initial share capital remittance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing foreign bank, confirmed by the receiving Egyptian bank or the Export Development Authority of Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; alternatively, a certified banker's letter delivered through the SWIFT channel may be accepted at the discretion of the Egyptian bank and GAFI

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, managers, signatories and UBOs against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Egyptian National Terrorist List issued pursuant to the AML Law No. 80 of 2002, and domestic politically exposed person (PEP) registers maintained by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU). Enhanced due diligence is required for any foreign PEP, family member or close associate of a PEP, and for funds originating from high-risk third countries. Continuous monitoring and periodic re-screening at least every 90 days are applied during the pre-incorporation stage.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (OSS) Investor Services Portal — https://www.gafi.gov.eg; Commercial Registry Electronic Filing Module operated by the General Department of Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be registered in the Arabic script. A Latin-character transliteration is accepted only for banking and cross-border trade purposes, and must be a phonetic equivalent of the registered Arabic name. The full name structure is: Trade Name (Arabic) + company form indicator 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company' (in Arabic: 'ذات مسؤولية محدودة'). Initials, numbers, or purely descriptive generic trade terms are not accepted unless forming an integral part of the actual trade name. The name must not violate public order, religious sensitivities, or existing trademarks in Egypt.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Investor Dispute Resolution Section within 15 business days from the date of the rejection notice. The appeal must contain the original rejection letter, an Arabic-language trademark search certificate, and a brief statement of reasons. GAFI must respond within 30 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may either submit a fresh name reservation with a distinct name, or escalate to the Administrative Court of Egypt within 60 days from the final GAFI decision. A name reservation may be extended for an additional 30 days by written request submitted before expiry, subject to confirmation from the Commercial Registry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office (without any physical premises in Egypt) is not accepted for the commercial registration of an Egyptian LLC. However, a business center arrangement with a dedicated physical address, a meeting room, and a local administrative agent is permissible for a wholesale trading LLC that does not hold physical stock in Egypt. For petrochemical polymers trading under ISIC 4669, GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority generally require a lease agreement for a physical office space and a visible signboard at the registered address. This is a medium-risk industry because the license implies significant transaction values.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% (Medium-High) risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections. GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority carry out periodic and ad-hoc field visits to confirm that the registered office is actively occupied and corresponds to the commercial license. The likelihood increases when the company files for high-turnover wholesale activities, engages in import transactions, or relies on a shared workspace.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) as amended, particularly Articles 118-133 governing Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 506 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department / One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Company Contract) submitted through the GAFI online portal or One-Stop Shop; final Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration Certificate. State filing fees are assessed in Egyptian Pounds by GAFI; no separate official USD tariff is published.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC under the Companies Law; the subscribers fix the capital in the Memorandum. The full subscribed capital must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or a notarized in-kind valuation report before the incorporation certificate is issued. No mandatory third-party escrow account is required under current GAFI procedure, but the funds must be held in the company's temporary pre-incorporation account pending issuance of the certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association as presented and subscribe to the share capital in the amounts stated therein. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is established at the address in the Articles and the individuals named as managers are appointed with the signature powers set out in the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the managers shall complete all statutory filings with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Tax Authority, and GOEIC; obtain the tax card, import/export code, and all municipal, fire and environmental clearances; open bank accounts; and execute any documents reasonably required to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / online company name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate name reservation form in Arabic and English with the proposed legal form 'Limited Liability Company' and the exact activity 'Wholesale trading of virgin polyethylene, polypropylene and other petrochemical polymers in bulk (ISIC 4669)'. The system runs a similarity search against registered companies and trademarks. Upon approval, reserve the name for the statutory period and proceed to notarization.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name-reservation application
Passport and national ID copies of all shareholders and proposed managers
Short memorandum describing the wholesale petrochemical trading activity
Lease or power of attorney for the proposed registered address, if already known
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a similarity conflict is found, submit up to two alternate names or add a distinctive Arabic transliteration; a GAFI name rejection may be administratively appealed within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the incorporation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public / GAFI-accredited legal office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic, setting out the LLC name, registered office, object clauses covering ISIC 4669 wholesale petrochemical polymers, capital, unit value, managers, and signatory powers. Have all founders sign before the Notary Public. Any in-kind capital contribution requires a certified valuation report incorporated in the contract.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Arabic draft of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Copies of shareholder passports and tax identification numbers
In-kind valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries inconsistent Arabic or English names, correct the Arabic text and re-authenticate; a substantive change requires a new notarized version before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription deposit and bank evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Egyptian licensed commercial bank selected by the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary pre-incorporation account in the proposed company name and deposit the full subscribed capital. Obtain a bank certificate stating the account holder, amount, and purpose. This certificate accompanies the GAFI incorporation filing as evidence of the LLC's paid-up capital.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract
GAFI name reservation certificate
Shareholder identity and KYC forms
AML source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires prior GAFI no-objection, request a preliminary GAFI clearance letter and resubmit; deficient AML documents must be completed by the shareholders or their attorneys before re-presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI statutory incorporation filing and issuance of incorporation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Companies Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation contract, capital evidence, and standard GAFI application through the One-Stop Shop or online portal. GAFI examines the legal form and object clauses, stamps the contract, registers the company in the Companies Register, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The file is then forwarded to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Passport copies and residence proof of shareholders and managers
Shareholders' resolution appointing manager(s)
GAFI application and beneficial-ownership declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, cure by filing a supplementary notarized declaration and corrected documents within 15 working days; unresolved objections may be referred to GAFI's complaints committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration, tax card, and import/export authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office; Egyptian Tax Authority; General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the GAFI incorporation certificate, register the LLC in the Commercial Registry of the governorate of its registered office and obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate. Apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for the Tax Card, VAT registration, and corporate income tax file. Register with GOEIC to obtain the import/export code so that bulk polyethylene and polypropylene pellets can be cleared through customs.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Notarized incorporation contract
Company lease or title deed and municipality letter
Manager passports and police clearance certificates, if requested
Commercial registration forms, tax forms, and GOEIC importer application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects the object or address description, amend the activity clause by supplementary GAFI filing and re-register; GOEIC objections are cured by updating the authorized importer manager details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises, civil defense, and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality and General Administration of Civil Defense
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the registered office and bulk-polymer warehouse, apply for a municipal occupancy/trade license and civil-defense inspection. Inspectors verify building structural adequacy, racking stability, fire separation, extinguishing systems, emergency exits, and housekeeping. Virgin polymer granules are non-hazardous in pure wholesale trade, so no environmental impact assessment is triggered, but the warehouse must prevent pellet spillage into drains and follow municipal waste handling rules.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate and tax card
Lease or title documents and floor plan
Civil Defense application and fire-safety equipment invoices
Manpower and insurance certificates if employees will work in the warehouse
Waste-management confirmation for polymer granules and packaging
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If civil-defense defects are listed, install the missing equipment or structural fire-protection measures and request reinspection within 30 days; if the municipality demands an industrial license, demonstrate pure trading and no manufacturing on the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for the commercial model of wholesale distribution of bulk petrochemical polymers; if a manufacturing license is ever sought, the competent authority would be the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) under Ministry of Trade and Industry procedures.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration Certificate; GOEIC Importer Registration; local municipal trade and occupancy license for office and warehouse premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure wholesale warehousing and distribution of virgin polymer granules without processing does not trigger an EIA screening category under Law No. 4 of 1994 and its Executive Regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply to the pure wholesale operation. The warehouse must control pellets and packaging waste to prevent spillage into stormwater drains, avoid open burning, and comply with municipal solid-waste handling rules and EEAA waste-management guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense fire-safety certificate for the office and warehouse, structural load inspection of racking and floors, emergency-exit and extinguisher compliance, municipal occupancy clearance, and Ministry of Manpower occupational safety and health clearance for any warehouse employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation of the LLC with the Commercial Registry (Companies Law 159/1981 or Investment Law 72/2017), the foreign shareholder(s) must (1) execute a notarized contract of association and obtain a commercial registration extract; (2) appoint a local tax representative if no physical office exists; (3) file the unified tax registration application (Form No. 1) with the competent local tax office (Mamouriya) or through the ETA electronic portal, submitting the commercial registration certificate, notarized board resolution and power of attorney for non-resident directors, passport copies, registered office lease, and bank reference letters; (4) obtain the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and tax card; (5) register for VAT under Law 67/2016 once annual taxable supplies exceed the statutory thresholds; and (6) activate e-invoicing credentials (ETA digital certificate, API/ERP integration, and authorized invoicing users) on invoicing.eta.gov.eg before first B2B invoice issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists in Egypt; an LLC is mandatorily taxed at entity level under Law 91/2005 at 22.5% corporate income tax on worldwide income while resident. Available statutory mechanisms: (a) simplified presumptive turnover-based tax at 0.5% - 1.5% - 2% under MSME Law 152/2020 if turnover and headcount thresholds are met; (b) VAT export refund election on quarterly or annual cycles; (c) foreign tax credit or tax-sparing election for foreign branch and dividend income; (d) group consolidation and hybrid mismatch elections are not available under Egyptian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations Decree No. 66 of 2017, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for supplies of goods; EGP 150,000 annual taxable turnover for supplies of services. Wholesale trading (ISIC 4669) is registrable once the EGP 500,000 goods threshold is exceeded. Imports of petrochemical polymers into Egypt additionally trigger customs VAT at 14% and applicable customs duties at importation, irrespective of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing: VAT-registered taxpayers must issue XML-based electronic invoices using ETA-approved software or ERP and transmit them to the ETA national e-invoicing platform (invoicing.eta.gov.eg) in real time (within 24 hours of issuance) for validation, assignment of a fiscal UUID, and QR-code stamping before delivery to the counterparty; e-receipts are being phased in for B2C transactions. Invoices not cleared through the ETA platform are non-compliant and input VAT credit is denied. ETA provides API integration and a taxpayer portal; violations attract penalties under Law 67/2016.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of polymers and other tangible goods qualifies for 0% VAT when the goods are shipped outside Egypt and the exporter holds a validated customs export declaration. Services rendered to non-residents may be zero-rated if performed and consumed entirely outside Egypt. The exporter must be VAT-registered, issue an e-invoice clearly marked as export at 0%, and evidence actual physical departure of goods from Egypt within the applicable statutory time frame.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration validated by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / road consignment note naming the Egyptian exporter as consignor
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate confirming receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency)
Fully executed export sales contract and commercial invoice
VAT e-invoice marked export and export packing list
Copy of ETA export registration or exporter tax card as applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export refunds are reviewed by the ETA refund department and are subject to documentary desk audits, customs-data matching, FX remittance verification, and on-site inspection. False or forged export documentation (fake bills of lading, circular exports, unrepatriated FX) triggers: (i) full clawback of the refunded VAT plus an additional penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded; (ii) daily late-payment penalties of 2% per month on any attributable unpaid VAT; (iii) criminal prosecution of the legal representative under Articles 76-79 of Law 67/2016, including imprisonment and fines; (iv) revocation of e-invoicing privileges and suspension from the exporter registry; and (v) potential application of the general anti-abuse rule with redetermination of tax on a look-through basis.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – Foreign Exchange Regulatory Unit and Banking Supervision Sector
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a liberalized current account payment regime for trade-related transactions, subject to documentary verification by authorized banks and compliance with CBE circulars. Capital account movements, including foreign direct investment equity injections and intercompany loans, are permissible after the investor obtains a GAFI (General Authority for Investment) certificate and registers with the CBE; statutory approval is generally automatic for standard trade and FDI flows but may be subject to periodic liquidity pressure in USD. Profit and dividend remittances are permitted for foreign shareholders after statutory audit of financial statements, payment of Egyptian corporate income tax, and submission of the bank's Profit Repatriation Form with the required supporting file; EGP is not freely convertible offshore, and all FX conversions must flow through CBE-authorized dealing banks. No material non-tariff hurdles exist for pilot imports of polyethylene/polypropylene granules, but the bank must verify the commercial invoice, customs declaration, and underlying purchase contract to comply with anti-money-laundering and anti-terrorist financing screening expectations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The CBE requires export proceeds from petrochemical and polymer transactions to be repatriated no later than 120 days from the bill of lading date. The full balance of the export invoice must be received into the exporter's foreign currency account maintained with an authorized bank in Egypt. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to Egyptian Pounds; however, the exporter must offer the export proceeds to the authorized bank at the prevailing market exchange rate if it wishes to sell such proceeds. The exporter may lawfully retain the export proceeds in a foreign currency account, provided that the source is supported by customs export entries, commercial invoices, and bank receipt statements. A failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline triggers CBE sanctions, ban of the exporter from receiving trade finance facilities, and potential inclusion on the CBE blocked list, unless a force majeure waiver is approved.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account, Foreign Currency Account, and Letter of Credit Margin Escrow Account
Operational Account and Import L/C Account
Operational Account, Foreign Currency Account, and Hedging Collateral Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for fully offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs). The Central Bank of Egypt requires any entity providing payment services or e-wallet/fiat custody in EGP or foreign currency to obtain a CBE license as a 'Payment Service Provider' or operate through a licensed bank. Offshore EMIs such as UK-registered and European-licensed Virtual Account Providers cannot be used as the primary operating bank because they do not satisfy CBE's onshore bank regulatory obligation for corporate treasury, cannot issue Egyptian LCs, and cannot serve as the authorized dealer for a capital contribution or profit repatriation. Offshore EMIs may be used only as an auxiliary collection channel for international card payments from low-risk customers, provided that funds are subsequently swept into Egyptian bank-controlled settlement accounts within 24 hours. The corporate treasury legal opinion should categorically forbid the use of any unlicensed EMI as the principal settlement rail for petrochemical trade.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the signatory directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the Egyptian LLC. Egyptian banks universally require a face-to-face interview at the branch before opening accounts for non-bank corporate entities, particularly for a medium-risk enhanced category such as wholesale petrochemical trading with ISIC 4669. Remote opening is limited to existing clients of the bank or branches of foreign banks that have executed a head-office guarantee and completed the KYC through an in-country correspondent relationship. For a new Egyptian LLC with 100% foreign ownership, the board of directors must pass a board resolution specifically authorizing the account opening and designating two authorized signatories. Passports of all legal representatives and UBOs must be physically verified by a CBE-licensed bank officer or a notary public in the jurisdiction of origin. Where a director cannot travel to Egypt, the bank will require an apostilled and notarized power of attorney naming a resident Egyptian agent, who must then appear physically at the bank branch for the KYC interview and biometric verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly established Egyptian LLC with a non-resident UBO and large initial trade volume expected in the first 12 months
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full suit: certified memorandum and articles of association, commercial registry extract ('sak almarkazi'), tax card, GAFI investment certificate, audited opening balance sheet, bank confirmation of the initial share capital contribution, UBO declaration, source-of-wealth statement, customer board resolution naming signatories, valid passports, utility bill proving the Egyptian registered address, and a detailed business plan for the import and distribution of virgin polymers with expected counterparty lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade geography or commodity classification may trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD) for the petroleum-petrochemical value chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the underlying international supply contracts and irrevocable purchase orders, customs classification documentation with ISIC 4669 and HS codes for polyethylene/polypropylene, cargo manifests and bills of lading, certificate of origin, mill test certificates from a reputable producer, and a description of the end-customer diversion controls. Banks will also require the company's AML/CTF corporate policy, sanctions-screening procedures, and a name-screening report of all buyers, sellers, transporters, and the vessel or trucking counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent beneficial ownership chain through multiple holding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full organizational chart up to the individual natural persons, corporate extracts from each jurisdiction, a formal beneficial ownership declaration that is CBE-compliant, and an undertaking to provide any further documentation requested under Article 15 of the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law (Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended). For a petrochemical trading LLC, the bank will additionally require recent audited financial statements of the corporate parent and, in some cases, a reference letter from the parent company's relationship bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential source of funds concern due to large initial inbound capital injection from the foreign shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a certified board resolution of the parent entity authorizing the injection, the share subscription agreement, a bank statement showing the source of the funds in the parent account, the SWIFT MT103 used for the transfer, tax clearance certificates, and a notarized declaration confirming that the funds originate from lawful commercial activity. If the funds originate from an offshore intermediate holding company in a non-FATF-compliant jurisdiction, the bank will require an independent legal opinion validating the capital ownership chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Egyptian LLC must be routed through the CBE-authorised dealing bank of the tier-one commercial bank relationship. The transfer must be made in US dollars or Euros using the SWIFT MT103 format with a proper purpose code: code '601' is applied to direct equity contributions by non-resident shareholders for the purchase of shares in an Egyptian company; code '201' is applied to pre-export and prepayment for imports; and code '901' for intercompany loans. The credit entry into the Egyptian bank must be matched within 30 days with the supporting documentation: GAFI certificate of incorporation, the LLC's commercial register extract, a board resolution of the foreign parent company, the shareholder's bank account statement, and the signed articles of association. The receiving bank must file a CBE monthly foreign currency position report and, if the total injection exceeds USD 500,000 equivalent, a special CBE capital-account notification must be lodged. The bank will verify the economic substance of the shareholder and confirm that the injection is not a disguised loan or monetary transfer subject to Central Bank licensing. The funds will be credited to the LLC's foreign currency account and may be converted to EGP only through the interbank system at the prevailing Exchange Rate for Commercial Transactions (ERCT).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary foreign trade disbursement rails for the petrochemical polymer distributor are irrevocable documentary letters of credit (L/C) and SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers. For the letter-of-credit rail, the Egyptian importer uses a CBE-authorised bank to issue an irrevocable L/C (MT700) in favor of the global producer, with the polymer granules classified as raw material and eligible for trade payment. The L/C will require the seller to present a full set of clean-on-board bills of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, shipper's certificate, and a chemical or polymer quality certificate. For sight payment, the L/C is typically drawn at sight via SWIFT MT700/MT710. For recurrent supply under open account, the Egyptian importer may use MT103 for settlement of goods already verified through customs, provided that the corresponding underlying invoice, customs entry 'Bayan', import license, and exchange control form are submitted to the dealing bank. All outbound transactions must be made against real trade documents to satisfy CBE's anti-money-laundering circulars; any advance payment above 50% of the invoice value requires a specific exception from the CBE if the payment is made before shipment. The Egyptian bank will settle payments in foreign currency using their correspondent banks in New York, London, or Frankfurt; thus the Egyptian LLC must maintain sufficient USD or EUR liquidity or purchase the currency from the interbank market using the registered commercial rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards for EGP/USD against confirmed trade receivables or payables with a maturity matching the underlying commercial contract
Foreign exchange swaps structured as USD/EGP against a genuine trade flow, permitted under CBE's guidance on hedging for real-economy companies
Cross-currency swap (USD/EGP) for the conversion of long-term intercompany loan liabilities, subject to CBE prior notice and consent if the maturity exceeds 3 years
Currency options on EGP/USD for hedging commodity-import price risk, permitted only when entered into with a licensed Egyptian bank under an approved master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for hedging Egyptian pounds offshore; onshore deliverable forwards are the exclusive lawful hedge

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19) and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax at 2% per month on unpaid tax from the day after the deadline; late-filing administrative fine under Law No. 91/2005; forced collection under Article 137; persistent non-filing triggers ETA enforcement listing and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements — Approval and Deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Companies Registry; ETA (attached to CIT return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end, aligned with the CIT return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers' joint liability and fines under Companies Law No. 181/2023; incomplete tax file invites ETA reassessment surcharge; GAFI may suspend registry certification and company records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before expiry of the previous tax card; renewal filed with ETA after the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating with an expired tax card triggers fines; suspension of bid/tender participation, license renewal, and customs clearance for import/export activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Commercial Licensing Office / GAFI licensing center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the issue anniversary; renewal application filed within 30 days of expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative closure of premises; daily delay fines; cancellation of the trade register entry after prolonged non-renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any direct or indirect ownership change and annually at the shareholders' meeting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law No. 80/2002 penalties — fines and imprisonment up to 2 years for false declarations; GAFI registry suspension; enhanced-scrutiny status under Medium-Risk AML classification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Audit and Endorsement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously updated; full verification at the annual shareholders' meeting within 4 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI inspection fines and director disqualification for incomplete Register of Shareholders, Register of Managers, or minutes; strike-off risk after administrative warning.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring — Monthly Payroll and Salaries Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, by the 15th of the following month (12 filings per year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax at 2% per month on unpaid tax; disallowance of salary expense deduction; criminal fine for non-withholding under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring — Monthly Value Added Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, on or before the last day of the following calendar month; e-invoice data transmitted continuously
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay tax at 2% per month; statutory fines under VAT Law No. 67/2016; denial of input VAT credit; suspension of e-invoice code issuance halting B2B sales.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring — Quarterly Withholding Tax Return and Remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter (4 filings per year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly 2% delay addition on unremitted WHT; payer held liable for the tax; profit repatriation and LC settlement approvals blocked pending ETA clearance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs, including EG_LLC, must appoint at least one auditor registered in the ETA's register of accountants and prepare audited financial statements annually; there is no size exemption under Companies Law No. 181/2023, and the ETA requires audited statements to accompany the CIT return in all cases.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), fully converged with IFRS; financial statements prepared in Egyptian Pounds; CIT, VAT, and UBO disclosures reconciled to the ETA e-filing and e-invoicing formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AML Law No. 80/2002 and GAFI UBO Registry rules, EG_LLC must identify every natural person owning, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the LLC's capital or exercising control, record changes in the UBO register within 30 days, and confirm UBO data annually at the shareholders' meeting cycle; share transfers involving bulk petrochemical trading counterparties are screened and reported under the same protocol.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per year for registered office and corporate agent services in Cairo or the Suez Canal Economic Zone
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,500 per year for an LLC wholesale trading entity with medium complexity and LC-based bulk sales

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic broad-based income tax holiday for wholesale petrochemical distribution. A registered LLC may apply for investment incentives under Investment Law 72/2017 through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), including a deduction of up to 50% of qualifying capital expenditure for projects in incentive zones for a maximum of 7 years. Entities physically located in licensed free zones of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) may benefit from prescribed free-zone exemptions, provided the activity is actually performed in the zone and export-oriented conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for juridical persons prescribed under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) InTax e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance income tax payments may be required for taxpayers above the ETA large-taxpayer threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a company using the calendar tax year ending 31 December, the filing deadline is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), legal form, registered address, fiscal year dates, and branch/parent entity details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian TIN registered to the foreign-owned LLC and state the Egyptian branch or POE address. Foreign parent details must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach audited local statutory financial statements, including income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Books kept in a foreign functional currency must be translated into EGP using the Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate at the balance sheet date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from wholesale trading of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, including export sales, domestic sales, and realized foreign exchange gains attributable to trading operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the local LLC or permanent establishment. Offshore title-transfer trades negotiated and executed entirely outside Egypt and not attributable to the Egyptian PE must be excluded from the income base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchase cost of petrochemical polymers, customs duties, freight, insurance, handling, and directly allocable import costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs must be supported by import documentation, underlying LC/SWIFT settlement records, and supplier agreements. Intercompany purchase prices must comply with the arm's length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative, selling, and distribution expenses incurred wholly and exclusively for the Egyptian business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if economically connected to the Egyptian LLC's PE. Head-office cost allocations must be substantiated and computed under the relevant PE attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses that are not tax-deductible: corporate income tax, late-payment surcharges, fines, bribes, entertainment exceeding legal limits, general provisions, and unsubstantiated cash expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident's share of head-office foreign administrative overheads is not automatically deductible unless supported by cost-allocation documentation and arm's length fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation on fixed assets used in the trading activity in accordance with the Income Tax Law rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only assets physically used in Egypt and owned by the LLC qualify for Egyptian depreciation. Assets retained offshore or used by related parties are not eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all transactions with related parties, including procurement from affiliated petrochemical suppliers, management fees, royalties, commission payments, and sales to associated regional distributors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled trading arrangements must be fully reported with the selected transfer pricing method and contemporaneous benchmark evidence. The ETA transfer pricing disclosure form is included with this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Taxable Income and CIT Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of adjusted taxable profit after add-backs, capital allowances, loss carry-forward, and incentives; application of the 22.5% statutory corporate income tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same rate applies to a foreign-owned LLC with a fixed place of business in Egypt. No reduced branch rate is available absent a specific investment-law decree.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for foreign tax credit under tax treaties and Egyptian withholding tax credits on Egyptian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign TRCs and statements of tax withheld in source countries. The ETA may require a revised filing if the foreign tax credit exceeds the Egyptian tax attributable to the same income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% on the unpaid assessed tax until full settlement, administrative fines for non-declaration, denial of loss carry-forward benefits where the return is not filed, and potential criminal prosecution for deliberate failure to file. The ETA may suspend the company's tax clearance certificate, which blocks imports, exports, and public tenders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The distributing LLC must withhold the statutory 10% at source. To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Egyptian Tax Authority: (i) an original TRC issued by the residence-country competent authority, (ii) a completed ETA DTA relief application declaring beneficial ownership and absence of a permanent establishment in Egypt, and (iii) supporting ownership and payment-flow documents. The ETA may issue a reduced-withholding approval; otherwise the payer must continue applying the 10% rate and the foreign shareholder may claim a refund through the ETA refund procedure. All treaty documents must be retained for at least 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and technical fees paid to non-residents is 20%; statutory WHT on interest paid to non-residents is also 20%. Under applicable double tax treaties, royalty rates are commonly reduced to 5%–10% and interest rates to 0%–15%, subject to TRC, beneficial ownership, and economic substance verification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 aggregate value of controlled transactions in a fiscal year; above this threshold, a contemporaneous transfer pricing Local File and the ETA transfer pricing disclosure declaration with the annual return are mandatory. A Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting obligations apply to multinational groups meeting higher consolidated revenue thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not currently operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the manner of UAE. However, the ETA applies substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, and anti-avoidance doctrines under Income Tax Law 91/2005 and relevant DTAs. A petrochemical trading LLC lacking real staff, physical functions, inventory risk, or decision-making substance risks recharacterisation as a conduit, denial of treaty benefits, and attribution of profits to the ultimate foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of trading revenue from polymer sales, use of fictitious procurement invoices, double-invoicing through offshore intermediaries, or inflating intercompany costs to shift profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to the proper taxable income, collection of the 22.5% tax undercharged, monthly 2% late-payment surcharge, and a criminal penalty equal to a substantial percentage of the evaded tax. Imprisonment and confiscation may also be ordered by the Economic Courts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved false returns may be personally liable for the unpaid tax, subjected to asset freezes and travel bans, disqualified from corporate management, and sentenced to imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting controlled purchases of bulk petrochemical polymers from related global trading hubs at prices outside the arm's length range without contemporaneous benchmarking, Local/Master File preparation, or ETA transfer pricing disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's length result, additional 22.5% corporate tax, monthly delay surcharges of 2%, administrative fines for failure to produce required documentation, and possible denial of corresponding adjustments for double tax relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for the adjusted tax where they knowingly signed inaccurate transfer pricing declarations. In serious cases, travel bans and criminal proceedings may follow under tax evasion provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the EG LLC as a bare re-invoicing shell with no inventory, staff, bank independence, office, or commercial decision-making; routing petrochemical margins through Egypt solely to access DTA benefits or preferential free-zone treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Piercing of the corporate veil; reallocation of income to the real beneficial owner; denial of treaty relief; cancellation of free-zone/investment incentives; and potential deregistration or liquidation of the Egyptian entity by the ETA and GAFI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution for diverted profits, disqualification from serving as directors in Egypt, travel restrictions, and possible criminal liability for fraudulent use of legal personality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing LC and SWIFT payments for petrochemical polymer shipments without adequate customer due diligence, failing to verify ultimate beneficial owners, deliberately concealing sanctions-related red flags, or repeatedly executing circular back-to-back LC trades with shell counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enforcement under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002 and Central Bank of Egypt AML directives: monetary fines, confiscation of funds, suspension of banking and trade facilities, revocation of licenses, and criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and signatories can be personally fined, imprisoned for up to 7 years, placed on travel bans, and subjected to asset freezes for failing to file suspicious transaction reports or knowingly participating in laundering trade proceeds.
